subject: Wellington Circle Redesign Study
overview: The commission welcomed three new members and voted to submit formal feedback on the state's Wellington Circle redesign draft report. The body also moved to re-submit a prioritized bike rack installation list to city departments and received updates on local paving and safety signage.

items.title: New Member Introductions
items.summary: Welcomed new commission members Mary Kate Gustafson, Noam Raveni, and Leah Grodstein, who shared their interests in improving local cycling infrastructure.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the June meeting.

items.title: Community Outreach and Route 16 Recaps
items.summary: Reviewed feedback from the Circle the Square event and a safety walk of the Route 16 corridor conducted with state representatives and local advocacy groups.

items.title: Bike Rack Priority Request
items.summary: Voted to officially re-submit the commission's prioritized bike rack location map to the Department of Public Works and the Traffic Commission to utilize racks currently in storage.

items.title: Summer Group Ride Planning
items.summary: Discussed organizing community rides and coordinating with a new Safe Routes to School task force to promote cycling for students and parents.

items.title: Wellington Circle Redesign Study Comments
items.summary: Voted to submit formal comments regarding the Wellington Circle draft final report, advocating for simplified navigation and signal timing that prioritizes non-motorized users.

items.title: MassTrails Priority Network Review
items.summary: Reviewed the MassTrails Priority Trails Network vision map and identified critical missing links in Medford's trail connectivity.

items.title: Infrastructure and Blue Bikes Update
items.summary: Received updates on the acquisition of state safety signage, ongoing street paving on South and Winthrop Streets, and the search for a Blue Bikes station location in West Medford.
